## Projects Department Health & Safety Standards

Ref:EGY/PRJCTS/HSE/REQs

- ●Ten percent of the on-Site workforce, on eachi shift, shall be trained in first aid treatment, and they shall always be readily available during the hours where work is carried out on-Site
- o All training shall be provided to an appropriate recognized and accredited standard and shall include CPR and other emergency techniques including triage
- All first aiders shall be suitably identified with a"Red-Crescent"Arm band/badge round the right upper arm, which shall be worn at all times on the Site ,In addition, there shall be provided and maintained so as to be readily accessible a first aid box or cupboard, a stretcher and a telephone for each satelliteSite.
- Inventories of all medical supplics and consumables held in first aid stations and boxes shal1 be held and regularly checked to confirm adcquatcly stocked.

## 2.4.3.4.3. Alcohol & Drugs:

- >Program Partners shall develop and implement a robust Drugs and Alcohol Policy.

## 2.4.3.4.4. Working in the Heat:

- Contractors shall produce aSummerWorkingPlan annually and submit toEMAAR Misrby the 1st May each year. This Plan shall identify all control measures and programs that shall be used to prevent heat related illness.
- Additionally, Contractors shall produce aRamadanWorkingPlan annually and submit toEmaar Misr which detail the control measures,including working hours.that shall be used to ensure the health,safety and welfare of those workers who are not eating or drinking in daylight hours.

## 2.4.3.5. Welfare:

## 2.4.3.5.1.Welfare at Worksites:

- Suitable and sufficientwelfarefacilities shall beprovidedfromthefirstdayon site,meeting the needs of all personnel. The guidance provided in Table 3 below represents Emaar Misr minimum standard.
- For sites and/or work which represent significant risks to health and where hygiene arrangements form part of the control measures,the risk assessment shall specify additional welfare arrangements as appropriate.

## >SiteWelfareFacilities
